name: board-home-draft
refs: HOUSING AND MATERIALS REFERENCE (the Companion, the Station's sibling: its matte sage-and-sand housing, dark rubber bumpers, screws, and its calm dark slate screen panels with cream text areas and orange for the one thing to do; take the materials and the calm, not its layout or its pixel-art creature):
THE KIT TEST (the Station's housing only: its sage-green matte shell, rubber corners, screws, braided strap and desk light; its blue glowing screen is a drift and must NOT be copied):
THE LIVING WORLD (Miniature Lives: sculpted, tactile creatures and a soft lit miniature landscape; take the craft and the warmth; no text):
PIP, the accepted creature: place it as it is, do not reinvent it:
LAYOUT SKETCH (rectangles only, ignore every fill, label and annotation):
prompt: Output a NEW image: a concept painting, 16:9, of the SCREEN of a rugged handheld field instrument, seen perfectly flat on to the viewer and filling the whole canvas edge to edge: the screen content, with only a slim strip of the device's own housing along the canvas edges (matte sage-green and sand powder-coat, dark rubber corner bumpers, a few visible screws, engraved blank plates). No photograph of a device in a room, no table, no hands, no perspective on the housing. Same maker, same materials and the same light as the references: matte textured sage and sand housing, dark rubber, moulded polymer, canvas, braided hose, worn paper; MATTE, never glossy; one soft warm daylight key light from the top left. On screen: calm dark matte slate panels with crisp cream-coloured blank text areas (leave clear empty slots where type will go); a single small orange mark for the one thing to do; lamps and gauges small. ABSOLUTELY NO text, no letters, no digits, no logos, no readable symbols anywhere in the picture. NO glowing blue HUDs, no holograms, no neon, no scan lines, no chrome, no polished glass, no gloss, no brushed metal cabinetry, no sterile white lab, nothing childish or toy-like. It must feel supportive of life and cozy, but visibly tethered to the working equipment that keeps the life going: feed lines, water and air lines, vents, small gauges and lamps that tend; worn, practical, carried and looked after. FRAME: HOME. Layout as in the attached layout sketch (take its rectangles ONLY, none of its fills, boxes or text): a large vivarium panel at the left taking about two thirds of the screen, and a column of four stacked section modules at the right. The vivarium window is the only warm field on the screen, set in the housing like a window in field gear, never a showcase: a living miniature world at the creatures' scale, lit by warm daylight from the upper left and a pair of small grow lamps on a bar above: moss, small stones, roots, a little water, low plants and a burrow, soft depth behind. Living in it: Pip (the attached creature, placed exactly as in the reference: the squat dark charcoal four-legged creature with a cream belly, orange eyes with cream rings and three small green leaves on its head; do not redraw it differently) standing in the foreground, and two or three other small sculpted creatures of other kinds going about their routines (a rounded coral-red lidded pot-shaped one, a teal long-tailed one with a glowing yellow tail bulb). The life-support equipment meets the window's edges: a feed line, a small mister, a vent, a small lamp. The right column: four dark slate modules, each holding one small object: a bay with fitted sample crates, a pod rack with six wells, an incubator dome with a row of small leaf lamps, a probe in its cradle with small plates; one small orange lamp.
